gen_risks.description: Extreme weather events and natural disasters, such as severe floods, cyclones, and extreme heat, could cause school closures, physical damage to educational infrastructure, and disruptions to instructional time.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate climate-resilient designs into classroom and childcare construction, including elevated foundations, LED lighting, solar panels, rainwater harvesting, passive cooling, and EdTech platforms to support remote learning continuity.
gen_risks.evidence: Paragraph 12: Natural disasters caused by climate change, including floods, cyclones, and extreme heat, pose significant challenges for Cambodia, particularly affecting the continuity of education.

gen_risks.description: Overloaded financial management staff at the Directorate General of Administration and Finance could lead to delays in processing financial transactions and issuing financial reports.
gen_risks.mitigation: Appoint adequate financial management staff, including government officers and qualified consultants, within three months of project signing as specified in the project implementation plan.
gen_risks.evidence: Paragraph 63: The current FM staff at the Directorate General of Administration and Finance may be overloaded, potentially leading to delays in processing transactions and reporting.

gen_risks.description: Delays in approving the Annual Work Plan and Budget (AWPB) could impede the timely execution of planned project activities across all components.
gen_risks.mitigation: Adopt a simplified AWPB template and standardized content guidelines in the Financial Management Manual (as part of the POM) to streamline internal review and approval workflows.
gen_risks.evidence: Paragraph 63: The delayed approval of the Annual Work Plan and Budget (AWPB) may hinder the timely implementation of project activities.

gen_risks.description: School mentoring funds disbursed directly to cluster lead primary schools may suffer from inadequate monitoring and fiduciary control at the decentralized level.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop and enforce specific guidelines on School Mentoring Funding embedded within the POM and conduct regular internal audits and financial monitoring visits by MoEYS.
gen_risks.evidence: Paragraph 63: There is a risk that school mentoring funding, which is to be spent at the schools, may not be properly monitored.

gen_risks.description: Limited knowledge and experience among MoEYS staff regarding World Bank Procurement Regulations could cause noncompliance and procurement execution delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Assign at least one dedicated full-time government procurement officer to the project and provide targeted World Bank contract management and procurement training.
gen_risks.evidence: Paragraph 68: MoEYS staff’s limited knowledge and experience with the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations, potentially resulting in project implementation delays and noncompliance...

gen_risks.description: Delays in receiving technical inputs and specifications from technical departments could slow down procurement processes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish formal coordination mechanisms between technical departments and the Procurement Unit, designating technical focal points to ensure timely submission of terms of reference and specifications.
gen_risks.evidence: Paragraph 68: possible delays in receiving technical inputs for procurement...

gen_risks.description: Governance vulnerabilities and potential corrupt practices in procurement processes could compromise contract integrity and resource allocation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enhance disclosure by publishing annual procurement plans and contract awards online and in newspapers, and implement a robust procurement complaint handling mechanism.
gen_risks.evidence: Paragraph 68: governance risks, including corrupt practices in procurement...

gen_risks.description: Inadequate capacity for contract supervision and management may lead to poor quality of deliverables and civil works construction delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide specialized contract management training to the procurement and engineering teams, establish explicit service standards in the POM, and deploy procurement tracking forms.
gen_risks.evidence: Paragraph 68: inadequate capacity for contract supervision and management, which may result in implementation delays...

gen_risks.description: Bottlenecks in internal clearances from the Procurement Review Committee could delay contract approvals and project effectiveness.
gen_risks.mitigation: Define clear service-level standards and turnaround times in the Project Operations Manual and delegate appropriate decision-making authority to evaluation committees.
gen_risks.evidence: Paragraph 68: possible delays in internal clearance from procurement review committee.

gen_risks.description: Transitioning Early Grade Learning and targeted instruction programs from small donor pilots to nationwide scale through government systems faces implementation fidelity, technical capability, and political economy constraints.
gen_risks.mitigation: Adopt an implementation science-informed learning agenda to rapidly test, evaluate, and adapt implementation features, using feedback loops to adjust activities in real time.
gen_risks.evidence: Paragraph 35: Transitioning from successful, donor-funded interventions... to implementation at scale through government systems requires overcoming technical, financial, political economy, and capability constraints...

gen_risks.description: Modernization of the Human Resource Management Information System (HRMIS) under Phase 2 may fail if Phase 1 scoping, technical feasibility, and cross-ministerial regulatory alignment with the Ministry of Civil Service are not achieved.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a joint inter-ministerial working group between MoEYS and MCS during Phase 1 to ensure technical alignment with the national MCS HRMIS roadmap before committing to Phase 2 firm recruitment.
gen_risks.evidence: Paragraph 41: Progression to Phase 2 is conditional on Phase 1 results demonstrating quality and feasibility in terms of technical development, alignment, and sustainability.

gen_risks.description: Civil works for new classrooms, preschools, and childcare centers could cause land acquisition or temporary land use restrictions affecting local property owners or occupants.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply the Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF) and Resettlement Framework to screen site choices, prioritize existing public land, and implement voluntary land donation or compensation protocols.
gen_risks.evidence: Datasheet: ESS 5: Land Acquisition, Restrictions on Land Use and Involuntary Resettlement - Relevant.

gen_risks.description: Project interventions and educational materials may fail to adequately reach or serve indigenous populations and ethnic minority communities in remote regions.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement the Indigenous Peoples Planning Framework (IPPF) to ensure culturally appropriate consultations, inclusive targeting, and adaptation of learning materials for indigenous communities.
gen_risks.evidence: Datasheet: ESS 7: Indigenous Peoples/Sub-Saharan African Historically Underserved Traditional Local Communities - Relevant.

gen_risks.description: Prevalence of gender-based violence (GBV) and sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment (SEA/SH) in project areas could pose safety risks for students, teachers, and workers during construction and service delivery.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct GBV/SEA/SH awareness training for public primary teachers and construction staff, establish a dedicated SEA/SH grievance redress mechanism, and enforce worker codes of conduct.
gen_risks.evidence: Paragraph 57: 10 percent of women ages 15–49 have experienced physical violence since the age of 15, and 3 percent have faced sexual violence.

gen_risks.description: Prevalent classroom overcrowding (classes exceeding 50 students) impedes individual instruction, behavioral monitoring, and foundational learning progress.
gen_risks.mitigation: Target infrastructure investments directly to severely overcrowded primary schools with 50+ students per class to construct additional climate-resilient classrooms and reduce class size density.
gen_risks.evidence: Paragraph 37: 76 percent of primary students learning in classes with more than 30 students... large classes are affecting student learning.

gen_risks.description: Inadequate access to quality early childhood care and education leads to poor school readiness among Grade 1 entrants, undermining primary education learning outcomes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Construct 60 public childcare centers and 60 formal ECE classes, support 500 community preschools, and run school readiness pilots in remote districts lacking preprimary facilities.
gen_risks.evidence: Paragraph 9: limited readiness among children to learn, resulted from inadequate access to quality childcare and early childhood education services.

gt_risks.description: Environment and Social risk is rated Substantial due to (a) limited institutional capacity to manage environmental and social risks and impacts; (b) nationwide implementation of the project's activities; (c) possible exclusion of vulnerable groups (such as poor children, children with disabilities, and indigenous groups); and (d) other risks involving child protection, occupational health and safety, labor issues, and sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment (SEA/SH).
gt_risks.mitigation: The project will develop a capacity-building plan for the Environmental and Social Safeguards Office and Project Management Unit, including hiring dedicated environmental and social specialists and providing targeted training. It will establish robust monitoring mechanisms to ensure support for vulnerable groups (universal design in new school/WASH construction, materials adapted for visually impaired students), strict adherence to worker codes of conduct, complaint redress and referral mechanisms, and construction site safety measures to protect school children and communities from labor influx and construction-related risks.
